clue.text: Play to make rings around the novices

indicators.note: the rings are placed on either side, enclosing the words that follow

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O, so two rings give two Os
taken as written
L is a learner, so two novices give LL

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to stage a drama that runs rings round the beginners.
explanation.walkthrough: Two Os ('rings') go either side of THE plus LL (learner plates, for novices).
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy of the Moor of Venice is a play.

clue.text: Sally pushing forward

explanation.surface: Someone named Sally is pushing ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden charge or sortie; the word also means a forward surge or rush.

clue.text: Word of praise for the choir

definitions.text: Word of praise for the choir

parts.words: Word of praise for the choir
parts.note: a liturgical shout of adoration sung by church singers, as in Palm Sunday anthems

explanation.surface: Someone compliments the singers.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Hebrew exclamation of praise to God, often sung in choral music.

clue.text: Obtain a University grant for a car

parts.note: to land something is to obtain it, as with a job
to let is to allow or grant

explanation.surface: A student secures a university grant to buy a car.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an early motor car body with a folding hood over the rear seats.

clue.text: Leave standing miles from home?

explanation.surface: Someone races off, leaving others far behind and miles from home.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a whimsical reading: OUT DISTANCE, a long way out.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip someone is to leave them standing; jokingly, 'out' plus 'distance' suggests being far away.

clue.text: Is now the two hours"______ of our stage " (R. and J.)

definitions.text: Is now the two hours"______ of our stage " (R. and J.)

parts.words: Is now the two hours"______ of our stage " (R. and J.)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from the Chorus's prologue to Romeo and Juliet, where the missing word means the business or dealings of the play

explanation.surface: A line quoted from the prologue of Romeo and Juliet with one word blanked out.
explanation.walkthrough: The prologue reads 'the two hours' traffic of our stage': the solver supplies the missing word from the quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Chorus uses this word for the business enacted on stage over the play's running time.

clue.text: Rocky position of thespian with no billing

indicators.note: the following letters are taken away from the word for thespian

parts.note: a thespian is an actor
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: An actor in a precarious spot, left off the playbill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes AC (account, billing) from ACTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocky hilltop or crag is a high, stony place.

clue.text: Mount Dumas created for a soldier

explanation.surface: Dumas invented a mountain for his soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a holy mountain in Greece and one of the Three Musketeers in Alexandre Dumas's novel.

clue.text: As a follower of Wells, one loses nothing by being very advanced

parts.note: the American firm Wells Fargo has Fargo following Wells

indicators.note: the letter for nothing is taken out of the word one

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An H. G. Wells fan loses nothing by being ahead of the times.
explanation.walkthrough: Wells suggests H. G. Wells, but it is the bank Wells Fargo; 'loses' drops O (nothing) from ONE, leaving NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something much progressed, as an illness or a drunk, is said to be well along, very advanced.

clue.text: Kid girl she's an exotic lady

parts.note: to kid is to con, deceive
Tess is a girl's name, as in Hardy's Tess
the indefinite article, a

explanation.surface: A girl is kidding herself that she is an exotic lady.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian countess is a foreign noblewoman, an exotic lady to English eyes.

clue.text: A listening device for soldiers covering a hill

parts.note: RES is short for reserves, soldiers held back
ON can mean covering, as one thing lies on another
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: An eavesdropping gadget planted by troops dug in around a hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow body that amplifies sound by sympathetic vibration helps one hear, a device for listening.

clue.text: Home for this bird is by the railway

definitions.text: Home for this bird is by the railway

parts.words: Home for this bird is by the railway
parts.note: the breeding colony of this wading bird is named by adding RY, the railway abbreviation, after the bird's own name

explanation.surface: A bird has made its nest beside the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird's home is a heronry, which is the bird's name followed by RY (railway).
explanation.definitionFit: The grey wading bird nests in colonies whose name is formed from the bird plus RY.

clue.text: Old gentleman housed in a pleasant area

indicators.note: the letters are lodged inside the words that follow, spanning both

explanation.surface: An elderly man lives in a nice neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas is pictured as a jolly bearded old man.

clue.text: Raw materials used to make pottery

explanation.surface: A note on what goes into making ceramics.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an iron-bearing ore, a raw material, and also a hard white earthenware china.

clue.text: The positioning of players at the bridge table?

definitions.text: The positioning of players at the bridge table?

parts.words: The positioning of players at the bridge table?
parts.note: bridge players sit as North, South, East and West, a seating by compass points

explanation.surface: A question about where card players sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Positioning by the points of the compass, literally facing the East, is alignment by bearings.

clue.text: Small is better for training by second teacher

indicators.note: the single letter is placed beside the rearranged letters, at the end
the letters are put through training, drilled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A coach insists that compact is best when it comes to training.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a motto about training; 'training' is the anagram signal, and 'by' places the S for second at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: She trains the dancers of a ballet company, a teacher of dance.

clue.text: Peg put on drill area to get the right angles

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a golfer's tee is a small peg
a parade square is where soldiers drill

explanation.surface: A peg fixed on the parade ground to mark out right angles.
explanation.definitionFit: A draughtsman's T-shaped ruler is used for drawing perpendicular lines.

clue.text: Missing out on exercise

explanation.surface: Someone avoids their workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Omitting something is passing over it; jumping rope is also a form of exercise.

clue.text: One of a pair manipulated by Madame Defarge

definitions.text: One of a pair manipulated by Madame Defarge

parts.words: One of a pair manipulated by Madame Defarge
parts.note: in Dickens's A Tale of Two Cities Madame Defarge sits by the guillotine working wool with a pair of pointed tools

explanation.surface: Dickens's revolutionary handles one of a pair of implements.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame Defarge famously knits the names of victims into her work, using a pair of these pins.

clue.text: Composer denying no man is an island

definitions.text: denying no man is an island

explanation.surface: A composer disputes Donne's line that no man is an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Donne wrote 'No man is an island'; the country, unlike a man, is one. John Ireland was an English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: John Ireland was an English composer, and the country's name contradicts Donne, being an island.

clue.text: Information sheet from a small box for example

explanation.surface: A printed handout comes from a little box.
explanation.walkthrough: Box is the evergreen shrub, not a container: a small part of its foliage is the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed handout is a sheet of information; botanically, the term also means a small leaf, as on a box shrub.

clue.text: Shelter in filthy dwelling when it's raining and snowing

indicators.note: the shelter word goes inside the dwelling word

parts.note: a pigsty is a filthy dwelling
lee is shelter from wind

explanation.surface: Taking cover in a dirty hovel during foul wintry weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather that mixes rain and snow is wintry and slushy.

clue.text: Sensible things men hope an arrangement can be made for

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words can be put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Some men hope a deal can be struck for practical things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sensible' here means perceptible by the senses, not wise; 'arrangement can be made for' rearranges MEN HOPE AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Things perceived through the senses are observable events or facts, in the philosophical sense.

clue.text: Marguerite has a neat look

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so one is an ox
to eye is to look at

explanation.surface: A woman named Marguerite looks very tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' is not tidy but the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The marguerite is also called the ox-eye daisy, a white-petalled flower.

clue.text: The bird to show a yellow streak

explanation.surface: A bird turns out to be a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small game bird, and as a verb it means to flinch in fear, showing cowardice.

clue.text: A picture that's out of a periodical

indicators.note: the first piece sits outside the second, enclosing it

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'
a mag is short for a magazine, a periodical

explanation.surface: A photograph clipped from a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A likeness or representation is a synonym for a picture.

clue.text: A girl lies in disarray in monochrome painting

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A girl lounges untidily inside a black-and-white picture.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a technique of painting entirely in shades of grey.

clue.text: 24 revealed in follow-up

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to dog is to follow

explanation.surface: A picture is revealed in a sequel.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is IMAGE, in the sense of an idol worshipped as a deity; 'revealed in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A graven idol stands for a deity, so a worshipped likeness is a god.

clue.text: Death of an Olympian seen as a blessing

parts.note: an Olympian is one of the gods of Mount Olympus, so 'of an Olympian' is a god's
an end is a death

explanation.surface: The death of a Greek deity is welcomed as a blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as GOD'S END: the end of a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Something welcome that arrives as if sent from heaven is a stroke of luck or blessing.

clue.text: Lack of interest is a forbidding sign

explanation.surface: Apathy is a deterrent sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, no entering shows no one is interested; it is also the sign barring access to a road.
